entities.summary: Denis Hale Johnson was an American novelist, short-story writer, and poet. He is perhaps best known for his debut short story collection, Jesus' Son (1992). His most successful novel, Tree of Smoke (2007), won the National Book Award for Fiction. Johnson was twice shortlisted for the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction. Altogether, Johnson was the author of nine novels, one novella, two books of short stories, three collections of poetry, two collections of plays, and one book of reportage. His final work, a book of short stories titled The Largesse of the Sea Maiden, was published posthumously in 2018.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Denis Johnson's works, particularly Jesus' Son and Tree of Smoke, have had a significant impact on American literature, influencing generations of writers and contributing to the country's literary identity. His unique narrative voice and exploration of themes such as addiction, war, and identity have left a lasting legacy in the literary canon.
